title: Copilot Cowork: access Business Applications through Work IQ and use business skills
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, admin-installed default, consumption model and control operations are supported by the current Microsoft documentation. The changed cost-management references still support the spending-policy update call; one minor qualification should acknowledge the different App Access navigation in Microsoft's general guide. The cited pages opened successfully during this check.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Cowork access to Business Applications through Work IQ and Business Skills for enterprise processes.
claims.quote: Users can access Business Applications through Work IQ in Copilot Cowork and use Business Skills to complete end-to-end business processes grounded in their enterprise data and apps.

claims.claim: The listed products are Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365), Microsoft Dataverse and Work IQ.

claims.claim: All users is the default tenant audience.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select **All users**. This option is the default.

claims.claim: The audience options also include Specific groups and No users.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select **No users**. ... To provide access to a limited audience, select **Specific groups**, and then add or remove groups.

claims.claim: The quickstart uses a slightly different label for the tenant availability setting.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select **Manage**, and select the environment. ... Select **Settings** > **Product** > **Features**. ... Locate **Work IQ**. ... Turn on **Work IQ** if it's currently off.

claims.claim: Learn names Power Platform Administrator for managing environment participation settings.
claims.quote: **Power Platform Administrator** role to manage settings and assign other roles.

claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment setting; Work IQ environment Power Platform API settings; Work IQ pac admin settings. Opened manage-participation and default-settings; no matching API, CLI or PowerShell setting found.

claims.quote: If you set some apps to **Allowed** or **Blocked**, you don't need to remove the setting when the app access control feature is turned off to **Disabled**. There are no app restrictions in this environment.

claims.claim: App Access controls which applications, including Cowork, can access data in an environment.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.quote: Go to **Copilot > Cost Management**. ... Select the **Configuration** tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... The spending policy details fly-out opens ... **Spending limits**

claims.claim: The spending-policy request body can update periodLimit and perUserLimit.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `billingMethods`.

claims.claim: Spending policies govern selected services and user audiences.
claims.quote: Scope a policy to every user in the tenant (`allUsersSpendingPolicy`) or to selected groups (`selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy`). ... Configure per-service settings that govern or exclude individual AI services within a policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies support policy-level and per-user limits.

claims.claim: Skill sharing uses Share on the Business skills page.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select **Share** from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Government-related environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Nonproduction environments**: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: The plan to enable existing environments has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule. Check this article for updates.

claims.claim: Learn states Business Applications in Work IQ is unavailable in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: For US tenants using FedRAMP-accredited environments, enabling Work IQ might send data outside the applicable FedRAMP boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not grant additional access to business data.
claims.quote: Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.quote: Select your credentials. A number appears to approve your sign in request. ... Enter the number in the **Authenticator** app.

claims.claim: Business skills are user-owned by default.
claims.quote: Skills are user-owned by default.

claims.claim: Skills can be shared with everyone in the environment.
claims.quote: **General access**—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Security-role sharing requires both the shared-with security role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the **Skill Sharing Role**, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ can create and update business records.
claims.quote: For example, ask Work IQ to list records from an app view, show the details of a record, create a record with the values in your prompt, or update an existing record.

claims.claim: Users review proposed values and explicitly confirm a data-changing operation before submission.

claims.claim: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.

claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server:

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing skills with repeatable scenarios before broad sharing.
claims.quote: Test each skill with a repeatable scenario before you share it broadly.

claims.claim: Create and update are unavailable when the selected form has OnLoad, OnChange or OnSave JavaScript handlers.

claims.claim: Custom controls and subgrids are unsupported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.quote: The **Business skills** page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback. Use controlled test cases and any logs or traces provided by the agent experience to collect evidence.

claims.claim: Cowork uses a consumption-based licensing and billing model.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork uses usage-based billing. Access comes only from a spending policy that includes the user and selects **Cowork**.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits are the unit for participating usage-based experiences, making cost variable.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity packs can fund this consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription can fund this consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business context and Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task are attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: Business context accessed through Cowork contributes to Cowork consumption. ... **Copilot Cowork**: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.claim: Separately reported Work IQ API consumption is not a Business Applications-only breakdown.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A request may involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so task cost varies rather than being a fixed prompt price.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No per-task rate for Cowork requests using business context is published in the feature's cost documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Business apps plugin licensing Copilot Credits per task rate; 'Cowork' 'business context' 'per-task'. Opened understand-costs, plugins/cost-considerations and billing setup; these describe variable consumption, not a fixed business-context task rate.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn names no separate licence specifically for the Business apps plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Business apps plugin licensing; 'Business apps (preview)' 'licensing'. Opened cowork-work-iq, understand-costs, plugins/cost-considerations and Work IQ API licensing; no separate plugin SKU is named, unlike underlying experience licensing.

claims.claim: The Cowork feature page says experiences can vary with the organisation's apps, licences, policies and services.
claims.quote: Some experiences might vary based on your organization's apps, licenses, policies, and available services.

claims.where: controls[4].governs; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A spending policy covering Cowork can cap the covered consumption with policy and per-user limits.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services. For example, a group using Cowork. ... When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset

claims.claim: Underlying application services may continue incurring licence fees during consumption-based preview services.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The model-driven app's Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting must be Default or On.
claims.quote: For the model-driven app, the **Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps** setting (`m365copilotmodelappenabled`) must be set to **Default** or **On**.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the relevant environment, model-driven app and business data.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: Enabling an experience does not itself grant business-data access.
claims.quote: Enabling an experience doesn't grant access to business data.

claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.

claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a [Microsoft Agent 365](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365) license.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Business apps' 'copilotPackage'; Business apps plugin install Graph. Opened cowork-work-iq and copilotpackage-block; package action search results do not identify the Business apps plugin as a catalog package.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block controls availability of the entire MCP server.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server ... Select **Agents** > **Tools**. ... Select **Work IQ MCP**. ... To block access to the server, select **Block**.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether blocking Work IQ MCP also stops the Business apps plugin in Cowork.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Cowork' 'Work IQ MCP' 'Block'; Cowork Business apps plugin Work IQ MCP block dependency. Opened cowork-work-iq, manage-ai-experience-access and business-applications-work-iq; none explicitly ties the Cowork plugin to this server's availability switch.

claims.claim: The package block operation is a beta API.

claims.claim: Preview behaviour can change.
claims.quote: Preview offerings are provided *as-is* and may be modified or discontinued at any time.

claims.claim: Deactivation stops agents discovering or using a skill without deleting its content or version history.
claims.quote: To stop agents from discovering or using an active skill: ... Select a skill, and then select **Deactivate** ... Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history.
